title: Token-wise generated Mirror modulation
hypothesis: For a token sequence task whose teacher applies context-specific Givens transforms, an input-conditioned token-wise Mirror generator reaches near-teacher accuracy with lower complete payload and modulation compute than a matched FiLM generator and improves over a static code table on mixed-context token streams.
physical_object: Shared 16-32-4 token classifier applied independently to each token in a length-8 sequence; token context varies within each sequence.
mirror_coordinate: Four Givens angles generated from each token hidden state plus context one-hot; every token may receive a distinct code.
logical_multiplicity: Eight token functions per sequence with context roles varying token by token.

task.teacher: shared random ReLU base with one fixed four-angle Givens view per context
task.split: stratified token-level train/validation/test within each generated world

methods: same-input FiLM generator outputting grouped scales+biases

development.allowed_tuning: select only learning rate from preregistered grid

storage.authority: actual torch.save inference bundle bytes after reload

success_gate: All fresh worlds: Mirror within 2pp of oracle teacher and independent upper control; at least 1pp above static code table; complete payload <=80% of FiLM generator or <=0.5pp quality loss at <=bytes; generator active MAC <=1.5x FiLM generator.
failure_gate: Mirror fails near-teacher quality in >=2 worlds or FiLM/direct table matches or dominates at equal/lower actual bytes and generator compute.
boundaries: aligned synthetic Givens teacher only; no natural language claim
sequence context variations are not independent model capacity
no device latency or energy claim
fixed updates do not establish capacity
